submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R1 at the maximum allowed thickness of 6 cm. Radiator-R2 is rejected despite its high index because the humidity ageing test shows a 40% transparency loss, exceeding the 10% hard limit. Radiator-R3 passes ageing but has the lower index and gives less pion/kaon separation in the thickness scan. Among the ageing-qualified candidates, the simulated 10 GeV/c pion/kaon separation is maximized for Radiator-R1 at 6 cm and remains above the hard 3.5 sigma requirement.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Thickness scan over the allowed 1-6 cm range identifies Radiator-R1 at 6 cm as the best ageing-qualified option; increasing to the upper allowed thickness gives the largest photon statistics and the best simulated separation among candidates that pass the lifetime constraint.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Radiator-R1, Radiator-R2, and Radiator-R3; the recommendation is Radiator-R1.

requirements.requirement: The pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c must be at least 3.5 sigma.
requirements.evidence: The simulation scan for Radiator-R1 at 6 cm gives pion/kaon separation above 3.5 sigma at 10 GeV/c.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after a 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%.
requirements.evidence: ageing_tests.md reports Radiator-R1 transparency loss of 6% at 400 nm after the 10-year-equivalent humidity exposure, below the 10% limit. Radiator-R2 is 40% and is therefore excluded; Radiator-R3 is 3%.
The selected thickness is 6 cm, which is within the allowed interval.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
